Vital Space — AI-Powered Astronaut Health Monitoring

Protecting Astronaut Health Beyond Earth.

As humanity prepares for long-duration missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond, maintaining astronaut health becomes increasingly challenging. Microgravity, disrupted sleep cycles, psychological stress, and environmental hazards can affect astronauts' physical and mental well-being, while communication delays may limit immediate medical support.

Vital Space is an AI-powered health monitoring platform designed to make astronaut health tracking continuous, proactive, and accessible.

Our solution integrates simulated wearable sensors, real-time data streaming using Apache Kafka, and machine learning-based anomaly detection to identify unusual physiological patterns. An interactive dashboard visualizes health trends, while an intelligent health assistant provides informational guidance to support astronaut well-being.

Inspired by NASA research and informed by publicly available health datasets, Vital Space demonstrates how intelligent monitoring technologies could support earlier awareness of health changes during extended space missions.

Our mission is to empower astronauts with meaningful health insights, even when Earth is millions of miles away.
details:
Vital Space — AI-Powered Astronaut Health Monitoring

The Challenge

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to significant physical and psychological risks, including cardiovascular changes, sleep disturbances, stress, bone density loss, radiation exposure, and environmental hazards.

As astronauts travel farther from Earth, communication delays and limited access to medical assistance make independent health monitoring increasingly important.

Our challenge was to explore how intelligent technology could help astronauts recognize unusual health changes early and better understand their health during long-duration missions.

Our Solution

Vital Space is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring platform designed to bring physiological monitoring, environmental awareness, machine learning, and health insights into one integrated system.

Our solution combines simulated wearable sensor measurements, data processing, anomaly detection, health trend analysis, and an interactive dashboard.

Rather than simply displaying health measurements, Vital Space aims to help astronauts understand changes in their physiological indicators and recognize situations that may require additional attention.

How Vital Space Works

1. Scientific Research and Data Collection

We explored NASA's Human Research Program and publicly available datasets to identify important health and environmental indicators.

Our research included:

  • NASA RR-1: Environmental measurements related to temperature, humidity, and CO₂ aboard the International Space Station.
  • PhysioNet BIDMC: Physiological recordings including heart rate and oxygen saturation.
  • NHANES: Population-level health measurements, including blood pressure, glucose, sleep, and physical activity.
  • WESAD: Wearable physiological data relevant to stress research.

We also created synthetic astronaut health data to simulate mission conditions and test the platform's monitoring workflow.

These datasets were analyzed separately because they represent different populations, environments, and recording periods.

2. Wearable Sensor Simulation

Vital Space is designed to support smartwatches, wearable devices, and smart spacesuit sensors capable of monitoring physiological indicators such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, and body temperature.

For our prototype, we simulated sensor measurements instead of relying on physical hardware.

This allowed us to demonstrate the monitoring workflow and test how the system responds to changing health measurements.

3. Real-Time Data Streaming

We developed a data-streaming pipeline using Apache Kafka and Python Producers and Consumers.

The pipeline receives measurement messages, performs data validation and feature processing, and prepares the readings for machine learning inference.

This architecture is designed to support continuous monitoring and future integration with physical sensors.

4. AI-Powered Anomaly Detection

We developed experimental machine learning models using the Isolation Forest algorithm, an unsupervised learning technique that identifies statistically unusual measurements.

Our models include:

  • Physiological anomaly detection: Identifying unusual patterns in health-related measurements.
  • Environmental anomaly detection: Analyzing ISS temperature, humidity, and CO₂ measurements.
  • Population-level health analysis: Exploring unusual combinations of health indicators using NHANES data.

We also incorporated baseline comparisons and health trend analysis into our monitoring approach.

The system distinguishes unusual statistical patterns from confirmed medical conditions. Its alerts are intended to support health awareness rather than provide medical diagnoses.

5. Interactive Dashboard and Health Guidance

We developed an interactive dashboard using Streamlit to present health indicators, historical trends, risk assessments, and monitoring information.

The platform includes rule-based health guidance that helps astronauts interpret their measurements and understand potential warning signs.

Our prototype demonstrates these capabilities using simulated and historical data, while full live integration remains a future development goal.

Tools and Technologies

We used:

  • Python: Core programming language for data processing, system development, and machine learning.
  • Pandas and NumPy: Data cleaning, analysis, and feature preparation.
  • Scikit-learn: Isolation Forest anomaly detection models.
  • Joblib: Saving and loading trained machine learning models.
  • Apache Kafka: Streaming architecture for health measurements.
  • Streamlit: Interactive dashboard and user interface.
  • SQLite: Local data storage and management.
  • GitHub: Version control and team collaboration.

Our prototype relies on software-based sensor simulation and does not require physical wearable hardware.

Innovation and Creativity

Vital Space goes beyond traditional health dashboards by combining multiple monitoring approaches in one astronaut-focused platform.

Our main innovations include:

  1. Combining physiological measurements and environmental monitoring to provide a broader view of astronaut health.
  2. Using unsupervised machine learning to identify unusual patterns without requiring predefined anomaly labels.
  3. Incorporating baseline comparisons and historical trend analysis to support more meaningful interpretation of measurements.
  4. Designing a Kafka-based architecture that could support continuous data processing from future wearable sensors.
  5. Providing accessible visualizations and rule-based guidance to support astronaut health awareness.

Rather than treating every unusual reading as a medical emergency, our approach emphasizes contextual interpretation and further review.

Factors We Considered

Throughout development, our team considered several important challenges:

  • Communication delays: Astronauts may not always receive immediate assistance from Earth.
  • Limited medical resources: Health monitoring tools must support onboard awareness and decision-making.
  • Environmental conditions: Radiation, altered gravity, and confined environments can influence astronaut health.
  • Data reliability: Measurements require validation and careful interpretation.
  • Dataset limitations: Publicly available medical data does not directly represent astronaut physiology.
  • Safety and explainability: Alerts should be understandable and should not be treated as confirmed diagnoses.
  • Scalability: The architecture should support future sensors and additional monitoring capabilities.

Intended Impact and Future Development

Vital Space aims to support astronaut autonomy by making health information more accessible, understandable, and actionable during long-duration space missions.

Our current prototype demonstrates the technical foundation through simulated data, machine learning experiments, a streaming pipeline, and an interactive monitoring interface.

Future development will focus on connecting real wearable sensors, validating models with representative astronaut health data, improving personalized anomaly detection, and developing a fully integrated live monitoring system.

Beyond space exploration, similar approaches could support health monitoring in remote research stations, isolated environments, and locations where immediate medical assistance is limited.

Our Vision

We envision a future where astronauts can better understand their health throughout long-duration missions through intelligent, continuous, and accessible monitoring technology.

Vital Space — Keeping Human Health at the Center of Space Exploration.
